lines.text: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, but does not let him enjoy them, so a stranger does.
A man with a hundred children and many years, but no satisfaction, is worse off than a stillborn child, who has more joy.
Even if the man lives a thousand years twice over without enjoying his prosperity, all go to the same place.
All a man's labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied, and the wandering of desire is better than what the eye sees.

wrong_details.wrong: the wandering of desire is better than what the eye sees
wrong_details.true: what the eye can see is better than the wandering of desire

lines.text: Man cannot contend with one stronger than he, and no one can tell him what will come after him under the sun.
